source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The heart's natural pacemaker fires at:
questions.rationale: SA node 60–100; AV node 40–60; bundle of His and Purkinje fibers 20–40.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Conduction system (PDF p. 74)
questions.quote: The SA (sinoatrial) node is the natural pacemaker of the heart. It triggers 60 to 100 electrical firings per minute.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A heart rate of 70 and stroke volume of 70 mL give a cardiac output of about:
questions.rationale: CO = HR × SV = 70 × 70 mL = 4,900 mL ≈ 5 L/min.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Cardiac output (PDF p. 74)
questions.quote: C.O. = Heart Rate x Stroke volume

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which blood test is the best indicator of myocardial infarction?
questions.rationale: Troponin is the most specific and sensitive marker of myocardial injury.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Troponin (PDF p. 77)
questions.quote: Best indicator for myocardial infarction (MI).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Tall, peaked T waves and a widened QRS on ECG suggest:
questions.rationale: Hyperkalemia: peaked T waves, prolonged QRS; hypokalemia: U waves, ST depression, flat T.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 ECG changes (PDF p. 78)
questions.quote: Prolonged QRS Complex Elevated ST segment Peaked T wave

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on furosemide shows U waves on ECG. The nurse checks which lab first?
questions.rationale: U waves suggest hypokalemia, a common effect of potassium-wasting diuretics.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 ECG changes (PDF p. 78)
questions.quote: Hypokalemia U-wave

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: To read central venous pressure accurately, the manometer zero is placed at the:
questions.rationale: The phlebostatic axis (4th intercostal space, midaxillary) approximates the right atrium; keep the same position each reading.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Central venous pressure (PDF p. 78)
questions.quote: The level of the manometer is placed at the right, mid axillary, 4th ICS

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: With a pulmonary artery catheter, the balloon should be:
questions.rationale: Inflate only to read PCWP, then deflate to avoid pulmonary infarction.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 PAP and PCWP (PDF p. 79)
questions.quote: Inflate the balloon only for PCWP readings; deflate between readings.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After femoral cardiac catheterization, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Keep the extremity extended, maintain bed rest, apply pressure dressing and check pulses, color and temperature.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Cardiac catheterization (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: Immobilize affected extremity, in extension. To prevent bleeding and promote circulation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before a treadmill stress test, the client should:
questions.rationale: Avoid caffeine, tea, alcohol and smoking; eat a light meal 2 hours before; wear rubber-soled shoes.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Treadmill test (PDF p. 80)
questions.quote: Avoid tea, coffee and alcohol on the day of the test.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which event commonly triggers angina?
questions.rationale: The 4 E's: exertion, emotion, eating a heavy meal and exposure to cold raise myocardial O2 demand.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Angina pectoris (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: The precipitating events to angina pectoris are exertion, strong emotions, eating a heavy meal, exposure to cold

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How does anginal pain typically differ from MI pain?
questions.rationale: Angina is exertion-related, brief and relieved by rest and NTG; MI pain is severe, prolonged and unrelieved.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Angina pectoris (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: R-elieved by rest and Nitroglycerine

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which teaching about sublingual nitroglycerin is correct?
questions.rationale: Sit or lie to prevent postural hypotension; take up to 3 tablets 5 minutes apart; keep in a dark, airtight container.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Nitroglycerin teaching (PDF p. 84)
questions.quote: Assume sitting or supine position for several minutes when taking the medication.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client using a nitroglycerin patch is told to remove it at night to:
questions.rationale: A nitrate-free interval (usually overnight) prevents tolerance.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Nitroglycerin teaching (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: Nitroglycerine patch is removed during the night to prevent tolerance from the medication.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client reports headache after his first nitroglycerin dose. The nurse explains this is:
questions.rationale: Headache from vasodilation is the most common side effect, especially early in therapy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Nitroglycerin teaching (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: Common side effect during first dose of nitroglycerine is headache.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before giving metoprolol, the nurse should first check the:
questions.rationale: Beta-blockers can cause bradycardia; assess pulse (and BP) before giving.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Beta-blocker therapy (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: Assess pulse rate before administration of the drug. Beta-blockers may cause bradycardia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Propranolol is avoided in a client with:
questions.rationale: Nonselective beta-blockers like propranolol cause bronchoconstriction; they also mask hypoglycemia in diabetics.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Beta-blocker therapy (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: Propranolol causes bronchoconstriction and hypoglycemia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which antidote should be ready for a client on a heparin drip?
questions.rationale: Protamine reverses heparin; vitamin K reverses warfarin.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Anticoagulant therapy (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: The antidote for Heparin is Protamine sulfate.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When giving subcutaneous heparin, the nurse should:
options: Not aspirate or massage the site
questions.rationale: Aspirating or massaging causes hematoma; give deep SC, usually in the abdomen.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Anticoagulant therapy (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: do not aspirate, do not massage site of injection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which lab is used to adjust warfarin, and what is the usual target?
questions.rationale: Warfarin is monitored by PT/INR, usually target 2–3; heparin is monitored by aPTT.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Anticoagulant therapy (PDF p. 86)
questions.quote: Therapeutic effect of Coumadin is INR 2 to 3

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: On ECG, an area of myocardial infarction (dead tissue) shows:
questions.rationale: Inverted T = ischemia, ST elevation = injury, pathologic Q = infarction.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Myocardial infarction (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: pathologic/enlarged Q wave from the zone of infarction

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After MI, why does the client use a bedside commode rather than a bedpan?
questions.rationale: Bedpan use promotes straining (Valsalva), which increases cardiac workload; stool softeners also help.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 MI management (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: Avoid Valsalva maneuver. Use of Valsalva maneuver increases cardiac workload. Use bedside commode instead of bedpan.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After MI, a client may usually resume sexual activity when he can:
questions.rationale: Ability to climb one or two flights of stairs without symptoms is the usual guide.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 MI management (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: Resumption of sexual activity may be allowed once the patient is able to climb I to 2 flights of stairs without difficulty.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of death after acute MI?
questions.rationale: Dysrhythmias are the most common complication and main cause of death; continuous cardiac monitoring is essential.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Complications of MI (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: The most common complication and the most major cause of death among clients with MI is dysrhythmias.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Before elective cardioversion for atrial fibrillation, the client is usually given:
questions.rationale: Anticoagulation first prevents dislodging atrial clots into the circulation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Atrial dysrhythmias (PDF p. 89)
questions.quote: client is anticoagulated first before cardioversion to prevent release of blood clots

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How does cardioversion differ from defibrillation?
options: Cardioversion is synchronized to the R wave
questions.rationale: Cardioversion is synchronized (never on the T wave); defibrillation is unsynchronized, for VF and pulseless VT.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Cardioversion (PDF p. 95)
questions.quote: Electric shock is applied during the R-wave, never on the T-wave.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Before delivering a shock, the nurse's essential safety step is to:
questions.rationale: Use gel or pads and call 'all clear' so no staff touch the patient or bed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Cardioversion and defibrillation (PDF p. 95)
questions.quote: Give command ("warning chant") for personnel to stand CLEAR of the patient and the bed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: In two-rescuer CPR for an infant, the compression-to-ventilation ratio is:
questions.rationale: Adults use 30:2; for infants and children, single rescuer 30:2, two rescuers 15:2.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Basic life support (PDF p. 96)
questions.quote: Two—man rescue: 15:2

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A rescuer finds a lone adult collapsed outside the hospital. After checking responsiveness, she should first:
questions.rationale: For adults, activate EMS first (sudden arrest is usually cardiac); for infants, do 2 minutes of CPR first.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Basic life support (PDF p. 96)
questions.quote: When performing CPR outside healthcare settings in adults, make an emergency call first, then do CPR.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An unconscious patient may have a neck injury. To open the airway, the nurse uses:
questions.rationale: Use jaw thrust when cervical injury is suspected; hyperextension may worsen damage.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Basic life support (PDF p. 96)
questions.quote: If neck injury or cervical spinal cord injury is suspected, use jaw thrust.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Three weeks after MI, a client has chest pain that worsens with twisting and eases when sitting up, plus fever. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Dressler's syndrome occurs 1–6 weeks post-MI: pain worse with movement, relieved upright, with fever.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Pericarditis (PDF p. 97)
questions.quote: Sudden, severe chest pain that is aggravated by turning, twisting the torso and yawning, relieved by upright position.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds and hypotension (Beck's triad) indicate:
questions.rationale: Beck's triad signals cardiac tamponade; treatment is pericardiocentesis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Cardiac tamponade (PDF p. 97)
questions.quote: jugular vein distention, muffled heart sounds, diminished or absent pulse (Beck's triad)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An intra-aortic balloon pump inflates during:
questions.rationale: IABP inflates in diastole to boost coronary perfusion and deflates in systole to reduce afterload.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 IABP (PDF p. 97)
questions.quote: The balloon of the IABP is inflated during diastole

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding points to left-sided heart failure?
questions.rationale: Left failure backs up into the lungs: dyspnea, orthopnea, PND, crackles, pink frothy sputum.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Congestive heart failure (PDF p. 98)
questions.quote: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (PND) Orthopnea Rales/crackles

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client's apical pulse is 54 before scheduled digoxin. The nurse should:
options: Hold the dose and notify the doctor
questions.rationale: Hold digoxin for adult apical rate below 60 and notify the physician.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Digitalis therapy (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: If apical rate is 60 bpm and below or 120 bpm and above, hold the medication and notify physician.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on digoxin reports nausea and yellow-green halos around lights. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Toxicity: bradycardia, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and visual disturbances (yellow-green vision, halos).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Digitalis toxicity (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: Visual disturbances: yellow or green vision; halos/rainbows around the light

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which lab result increases a client's risk of digoxin toxicity?
questions.rationale: Hypokalemia enhances digitalis toxicity; check potassium before giving.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Digitalis therapy (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: Hypokalemia enhances digitalis toxicity.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why should furosemide be given in the morning rather than at bedtime?
questions.rationale: Give diuretics early (not after about 6 pm) to prevent sleep disruption from nocturia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Diuretic therapy (PDF p. 101)
questions.quote: Administer the medication early morning and/or early afternoon, not later than 6 pm.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on spironolactone should be taught to avoid:
questions.rationale: Spironolactone is potassium-sparing; avoid excess potassium (salt substitutes, high-K foods) to prevent hyperkalemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Diuretic therapy (PDF p. 102)
questions.quote: Advise the client to avoid potassium — rich foods.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with acute pulmonary edema is placed in high Fowler's with legs dangling to:
questions.rationale: Legs down pools blood in the extremities and reduces venous return to the failing heart.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Pulmonary edema (PDF p. 103)
questions.quote: High Fowler's position with legs lowered. To reduce preload.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which instruction belongs in teaching for a client with a permanent pacemaker?
options: Take your pulse daily on waking
questions.rationale: Check pulse daily, report changes, avoid contact sports and strong electromagnetic sources; prolonged hiccups may signal failure.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 4 Pacemaker teaching (PDF p. 94)
questions.quote: Take daily pulse for one full minute upon arising in the morning.
